name: FortiGate — VPN Brute Force From External Source
description: An external source IP generated 500 or more FortiGate VPN authentication failures in a 6-hour window — external brute-force against the IPsec VPN. FortiGate VPN failures carry NO user attribution (user.name and xauthuser both 0%), so this is necessarily a source-volume detection, not user-based. NBI's baseline is a persistent floor of ~4 loud external IPs (peaks 400-820 failures/hour) far above internet background (<1/hour), so the 500/6h threshold cleanly isolates real brute-force. Internal sources are excluded (RFC1918) — this is the external attack surface. Basic license does not enforce suppression, so a persistent source re-alerts hourly; the correct response is to block the source IP (which also stops the alert).
note:
### Investigation — external VPN brute force
1. **WHO / FROM WHERE** `source.ip` — an external IP hammering the VPN. Check geo/reputation; NBI's known persistent offenders include 185.217.76.86 / 193.122.51.47 / 185.112.188.197 / 130.193.131.98.
2. **DID WHAT** >=500 VPN auth failures in a 6h window against the FortiGate. No username is logged (IKE), so treat as source-level brute-force.
3. **WHY suspicious** volume far above background; sustained targeting of the remote-access surface.
4. **Escalate / act**: block the source IP at the perimeter (stops the attack and the recurring alert). Check whether the same source ever produced a VPN SUCCESS (would indicate the brute-force worked).

standard.rule_type_rationale: D0 observable = count of VPN failures per external source crossing a baselined number; no user attribution exists so cardinality-of-users is impossible; New Terms fires on ubiquitous internet background (23 new sources/day). D2 -> Threshold on volume. Baseline: 4 sources at 400-820/hr vs <1/hr background.

query: fortinet.firewall.subtype:"vpn" and event.outcome:"failure" and source.ip:* and not source.ip:"10.0.0.0/8" and not source.ip:"172.16.0.0/12" and not source.ip:"192.168.0.0/16"
